newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-U.Utils sees tax challenge unlikely.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-U.Utils sees tax challenge unlikely.

text.p: British multi-utility United Utilities would be "surprised" if any eventual one-off "windfall" tax proposed by the government were able to be challenged legally, chief executive Brian Staples said.
"I'll be quite surprised if the eventual tax is legally challengeable," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Staples said he thought "it very much comes down to the size of the tax...I think our reaction to it will be to look at it in terms of fairness and the way that it's applied," he added.

The new Labour government, which swept into power with a landslide victory on May 1, has vowed to impose a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities but further details will emerge in the government's first budget, possibly in June.
